## Breaking change

The Radio Thermostat integration has been migrated to configuration via the UI. Configuring Radio Thermostat via YAML configuration has now been deprecated and will be removed in a future Home Assistant release.

Your existing YAML configuration is automatically imported on upgrade to this release; and thus can be safely removed from your YAML configuration after upgrading.

@dmradcliff Can you show the configuration for your radiotherm component? ~What model of the thermostat do you have?~ Can you confirm that you can connect to the API (to do this, try going to `http://<ip of radiotherm>/tstat` in your browser or from the command line `curl http://<ip of radiotherm>/tsat`

The "socket.timeout" error you are seeing is usually indicative of an issue connecting with the thermostat (or else with your thermostat responding) and not an issue with home assistant.

> @dmradcliff Can you show the configuration for your radiotherm component? ~What model of the thermostat do you have?~ Can you confirm that you can connect to the API (to do this, try going to `http://<ip of radiotherm>/tstat` in your browser or from the command line `curl http://<ip of radiotherm>/tsat`
> 
> The "socket.timeout" error you are seeing is usually indicative of an issue connecting with the thermostat (or else with your thermostat responding) and not an issue with home assistant.


climate:
platform: radiotherm
host:
- 192.168.1.196
hold_temp: False

For your info, I timed the curl command and it takes a long time to reply.

time curl 192.168.1.196/tstat
{"temp":74.50,"tmode":1,"fmode":0,"override":0,"hold":0,"t_heat":70.00,"program_mode":-1,"tstate":0,"fstate":0,"time":{"day":6,"hour":16,"minute":28},"t_type_post":0}
real 0m 23.06s
user 0m 0.01s
sys 0m 0.01s

In case it helps
CT80 V2.34 T
Firmware version 1.04.84
API Version 113

Wow, 23 seconds. My CT50 usually responds within 2-3 seconds. You can try putting a long timeout in the `radiotherm` library setup by editing [this line](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/radiotherm/climate.py#L131):

From:
```
tstat = radiotherm.get_thermostat(host)
```

To:
```
tstat = radiotherm.get_thermostat(host, timeout=30)
```

That will be a very unresponsive component in Home Assistant.

I have one of the very early CT80 thermostats and I know they have improved them over time.  I remember back in the day reading that they suggested spacing out calls to the thermostat because it would overwhelm the processor and take a long time to do its normal tasks plus respond to external requests.

How do I make the edit you recommended?  I am running home assistant OS and haven't found a way to get access to the file. I can't seem to get outside the config, addons, backup, media, share, and ssl folders which are exposed through the SAMBA interface.

I'm not 100% sure for the Home Assistant OS, I think it's likely at one of these locations:

* `/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/radiotherm/climate.py`
* `/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/homeassistant/components/radiotherm/climate.py`

If it's not at either of those locations, should be able to find it using this command:

```
find / | grep 'components/radiotherm'
```
